Before Operto One, guest messaging was handled entirely through a cell phone. Every guest was manually entered as a contact, coded by their dates, phone number, and room number. At 1:00 AM, when a message came in, Dawn could glance at the screen and know whether the guest was in-house or arriving in three weeks, and prioritize accordingly.

The system worked because Dawn and her team made it work. They personally texted every arriving guest, tracked flights, and timed her messages to land the moment passengers stepped off the plane. But as Wharfside Village grew, three operational issues became impossible to ignore.
